GitHub step by step

Track changes to your repair café website, review a teammate’s update and publish a static site with GitHub Pages.

1. Repositories 2. Commits 3. Push and pull 4. Branches and pull requests 5. GitHub Pages 6. Project and troubleshooting

1. Create a repository

Git records versions of files. GitHub hosts repositories online so you can share the files and their history. A repository is a project with its version history.

  1. On GitHub, choose New repository and name it repair-cafe.
  2. For this publishing exercise, use a public repository containing fictional content you own or have permission to publish. Initialise it with a README.
  3. Copy the HTTPS clone URL from Code. In your terminal, replace YOUR-USERNAME below, then open the cloned folder in VS Code. 
git clone https://github.com/YOUR-USERNAME/repair-cafe.git
cd repair-cafe
git status
Check your understanding

Where can you make and commit changes while offline? In the local clone. A push needs access to the remote repository.

2. Stage and commit your first page

Add an index.html file with a title and the café opening hours. If Git asks for an author identity, set your name and a GitHub account email or the no-reply address from your GitHub email settings. Use the same commands without --global to apply them to this repository only. 

git config user.name "Your Name"
git config user.email "YOUR-EMAIL"
git status
git add index.html
git diff --staged
git commit -m "Add the repair cafe home page"
git log --oneline -3

The working tree holds your current files. Staging selects changes for the next snapshot. A commit records that snapshot locally with its message.

Exercise and expected result

Edit both README.md and index.html. Stage only index.html, then run git status. The HTML change should be staged, while the README change remains unstaged.

3. Push and pull changes

origin is the remote name created by clone. These examples assume the default branch is main. Check your branch name and use the one your repository actually uses. Sign in through your Git credential manager or an authenticated GitHub CLI session if prompted. 

git branch --show-current
git remote -v
git push origin main
git pull --ff-only origin main

Push sends local commits to GitHub. Pull brings remote changes into the current branch. Run pull from a clean working tree. The fast-forward-only option stops when the histories have diverged so you can inspect the situation before integrating changes.

Exercise and expected result

Edit README.md on GitHub and commit it. With a clean local working tree on main, pull. The README should update locally and git log should show the new commit.

4. Use a branch and pull request

Start on an up-to-date main branch. Use a feature branch to isolate a change. Add a venue section to index.html before staging it. 

git switch -c add-venue
git add index.html
git commit -m "Add venue directions"
git push -u origin add-venue

Open a pull request on GitHub with main as the base and add-venue as the compare branch. Describe the change, how you tested it and how someone can verify it. Review the Files changed tab. Merge after the change has been checked, then switch back to main and pull.

Resolve a simple merge conflict

If both branches change the same lines, inspect the conflict markers in the file. Agree on the final wording, remove the markers, test the page, stage the resolved file and finish the merge. Use git status to see what Git expects next.

Exercise and expected result

Open a pull request that edits the venue only. The diff should show that change. After merging and pulling, main should include the new directions.

5. Publish with GitHub Pages

  1. Check that index.html and its linked CSS and JavaScript files are committed on main.
  2. In repository Settings, open Pages. Under Build and deployment, choose Deploy from a branch. Select main and /(root), then save.
  3. Wait for the deployment and open the URL shown in Pages. For a project named repair-cafe, it normally follows https://YOUR-USERNAME.github.io/repair-cafe/.
  4. Test the published site on a phone and desktop. If CSS is missing, compare the linked path and filename case. Use ./css/site.css from the root page when your files follow that layout.

GitHub Pages serves static files. A form that stores submissions needs a separate service.

Exercise and expected result

Update the opening hours on main and push. After the next successful deployment, the public page should show the new hours.

6. Complete the repair café project

Submit your repository link, your Pages link and the link to a merged pull request. Include the opening hours and venue, a stylesheet and a README explaining how to run and test the website.

  • Push rejected. Run git status and git fetch, then inspect the remote changes before integrating them.
  • Pages shows 404. Check the deployment status, selected branch and folder, and exact index.html filename.
  • Styles work locally only. Check case, confirm the file was committed, and verify the CSS URL under the repository’s Pages path.

Read the GitHub Hello World guide and the GitHub Pages publishing guide.
